sections.text: We are a UL 508A listed panel shop in Brea, California with electrical and software engineers on staff. Send us a complete drawing package and we build to print. Send us a process and no drawings, and we do the electrical design in AutoCAD, modify the enclosure on our Hoffman Modification Center, build and test the panel, then write and commission the PLC, HMI, and drive code that runs it.

sections.heading:
Drawing, metal, and code —
all of it happens here
sections.intro: Most panel shops do one of these three well and buy the other two. That's why schedules slip: the enclosure comes back from a fab shop cut wrong, or the panel is finished and then sits waiting on a programmer who has never seen it. We do all three in this building, and the same people stay on your job from the first drawing to the day it runs.

sections.heading: How a panel job runs
sections.intro: Five stages. You get a named contact and a scheduled checkpoint at each one — not a quote and then silence until shipping.

items.label: Stage 01
items.title: Quote
items.text: We review your package, flag anything that will drive cost or lead time, and quote with a fixed component list.

items.label: Stage 02
items.title: Engineering
items.text: AutoCAD schematics, layout, heat rise, SCCR, and BOM by our own electrical engineers. You approve drawings before we cut metal.

items.label: Stage 03
items.title: Fabricate
items.text: Enclosure machined on our Hoffman ModCenter to the released drawing. Components ordered from authorized distributors only.

items.label: Stage 04
items.title: Build and test
items.text: Wire, label, then 100% point-to-point check and a powered functional test running the actual PLC code against your sequence.

items.label: Stage 05
items.title: Commission
items.text: Our software engineers start it up on your floor, tune the drives, and train your operators and maintenance team.

sections.heading:
One purchase order.
Four shops.
sections.text: Most panel builders subcontract their machining and buy their harnesses. When something doesn't fit, you're the one managing three vendors pointing at each other. We do all four in house — so the harness was built for that panel, and the back panel was cut for that enclosure.

items.q: What actually drives the price of a control panel?
items.a: Components, almost always. The enclosure, drives, PLC, and safety devices typically make up the majority of the cost, and labor is a smaller share than most buyers expect. That's why we quote against a fixed component list — so you can see what's driving the number and decide whether a different drive or enclosure is worth the change.

items.q: Can you apply the UL label, or do I need a field evaluation?
items.a: We apply it. As a UL 508A listed shop we build under our own file and the panel ships with the label already on it. Field evaluations are what you need when a panel was built by someone who isn't listed, and they typically add cost and schedule per panel.

items.q: What is SCCR and why does my inspector care about it?
items.a: Short circuit current rating is the maximum fault current the panel can safely withstand. It has to be marked on the panel and it has to be at least as high as the available fault current at the point of installation. It's one of the most common reasons a panel gets red-tagged, so we calculate it during design rather than discovering it at startup.

items.q: Do you program the panel, or just build it?
items.a: Either. We have software engineers on staff, so we can deliver the panel with the PLC, HMI, and drive code written, tested on the bench, and commissioned on your floor. Plenty of customers do their own programming and just want the hardware — that's fine too, and it's quoted separately so you're not paying for engineering you don't need.

items.q: Which industrial networks can you work with?
items.a: EtherCAT, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, PROFIBUS, and Modbus TCP and RTU, including mixed architectures where a machine has to talk to equipment on more than one protocol. If your plant standard is one network and a piece of vendor equipment arrives on another, that's a routine problem here rather than a change order.

items.q: Do I own the PLC program?
items.a: Yes. Source code is delivered unlocked and documented along with schematics, CAD files, and the operator manual. You are not required to come back to us to make a change — though we're happy to be the ones who do it.

items.q: Will you build from drawings another shop produced?
items.a: Yes, that's Path A. We'll review the package first and tell you if we see anything that won't pass UL or won't work as drawn, but we don't require you to pay us to redraw someone else's design.
